title: Rollforward safety controller with cost-aware automatic triggers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current rollback triggers are largely binary and tuned by hand; teams either revert too quickly (false positives) or wait too long (false negatives), and token cost / throughput signals are rarely considered in an integrated way. Goal: Deliver a Rollforward Safety Controller that decides both safe rollback and safe rollforward (increasing traffic) actions using multi-signal SLO reasoning that includes latency, error rate, token cost per request, and throughput. The controller must be tunable, simulator-backed, and expose transparent scoring for operator review.

Design summary: The controller computes a multi-signal health score per cohort using normalized anomaly scores (z-score or nonparametric rank transforms) over sliding windows. Signals: latency p95, request error rate, tokens/request, effective throughput (requests/sec). Each signal is mapped to a risk score in [0,1]; an aggregate risk is a weighted sum where weights are configurable per-customer and per-environment (default weights favor latency and error rate).

Thresholds / auto-tuning: thresholds are defined as probabilistic bands rather than static points. We compute a baseline distribution using a 28-day rolling window with seasonality-aware detrending. Alerts/trigger bands use Bayesian credible intervals: trigger when the posterior probability that metric > baseline + delta exceeds a configurable alpha (default alpha=0.975). A separate band for rollforward requires sustained improvement (posterior probability of improvement > 0.99 over a minimum duration).

Adaptive tuning: The system will run an online calibration step using multi-armed bandit logic over historical rollout outcomes to recommend adjusted signal weights and alpha/holdout durations per workload. Calibration runs in the background and surfaces suggested adjustments; operators can accept or schedule automatic application.

Failure modes & safety layers: - Cooldown window: once an action occurs (rollback or rollforward), a cooldown of configurable minutes prevents flip-flopping. - Minimum sample constraints: require N requests and minimum active cohorts to compute statistics. - Cohort isolation: decisions computed per-cohort + global aggregator for safety (global override if many cohorts degrade simultaneously). - Cost-aware override: token-cost-per-request is treated as a first-class signal; if cost per token skyrockets but latency/error remain acceptable, the controller surfaces a mitigation recommendation (rate limit, reroute, quantized fallback) but will not auto-rollback unless other signals concur.

Actions: automatic rollback (traffic moved to previous model variant), auto-rollforward (increase canary %), partial traffic split rebalancing, and operator-facing recommendations. Each action emits events to audit log and sends an incident-like page when thresholds for severity met.

Telemetry & observability: Add metric exporters for per-cohort risk score, posterior probabilities, and action history. New console dashboard: "Rollforward Safety" with heatmap of cohorts, time-series of signals, action timeline, and calibration recommendations. Links: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.com/confluence/rfd-rollforward-safety (placeholder), simulation notebook: https://drive.redwood.com/sim/rollforward-sim-2026 (placeholder).

Simulation results (summary): on historical canaries across 14 production rollouts, proposed Bayesian banding reduced false-rollbacks by ~62% and detected true degradations within median 3 minutes (vs 7 minutes baseline) when traffic >= 1% and request volume > 2k/min. Cost-aware recommendations helped avoid 3 high-cost rollbacks by suggesting quantized fallbacks. Details in notebook.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Controller deployed to staging and validating on 1% canaries; 2) Dashboard shows correct risk score and posterior metrics and action events; 3) Simulation benchmark reproducible and FPR/TPR reported; 4) End-to-end audit events in customer log and PRs merged.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout; stage -> internal canaries (1%) -> beta customers (5%) -> gradual ramp with automatic cooldown monitoring.

Runbook excerpt: emergency revert: disable controller via feature flag, manually migrate canaries using Console route controls, and inspect audit timeline.
